scholarships.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Cape Town (2027 intake, postgraduate)

existing.description: A fully funded scholarship and support programme for African students at the University of Cape Town, delivered in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation. Applicants must be citizens of an African country and must face significant social and economic barriers to accessing higher education; UCT states it encourages applications from young women, people living with disabilities, refugees and forcibly displaced youth. It covers a first bachelor's degree, a postgraduate diploma in the Faculty of Health Sciences, an honours degree or a coursework master's degree at UCT, but not part-time study or research-only degrees.
eligibility: Be a citizen of an African country, including South Africa

Be applying for a first bachelor's degree, or for a UCT postgraduate diploma offered by the Faculty of Health Sciences, an honours degree offered by any of UCT's six faculties, or a coursework master's programme offered by any of UCT's six faculties
Demonstrate academic talent and a commitment to excellence
Face significant social and economic barriers to accessing higher education
Demonstrate potential for transformative and ethical leadership
Be committed to serving their communities and contributing to positive change
Only applicants who receive an offer of admission to UCT are eligible for the programme
existing.eligibility_summary: Citizens of any African country who face significant social and economic barriers to higher education and are applying for a first bachelor's degree, a UCT postgraduate diploma in the Faculty of Health Sciences, an honours degree, or a coursework master's degree. UCT explicitly encourages applications from young women, people living with disabilities, refugees and forcibly displaced youth.
benefits: Scholarship and comprehensive academic, psychosocial and financial support
Membership of the Mastercard Foundation Scholars alumni network
requirements: Admission application submitted to the University of Cape Town
Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application submitted separately
Evidence of significant social and economic barriers to higher education
documents: UCT admission application and supporting academic documents
Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application form
Academic transcripts and prior study records as required by the chosen UCT faculty
application_method: STEP 1 - review UCT study options at https://uct.ac.za/applicants-and-students
STEP 2 - submit the UCT admission application at applyonline.uct.ac.za
STEP 3 - submit the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application at https://uct.ac.za/mastercardfdn
existing.selection_notes: UCT selection criteria: academically talented with a demonstrated commitment to learning and a drive to complete the education; limited in the ability to access education owing to significant financial barriers; committed to investing in the community through acquired skills; a future leader committed to ethical transformation. Acceptance of admission at UCT alone does not guarantee selection for the programme.
existing.best_fit: African students who are financially excluded from higher education, including first-degree students, women, students with disabilities and refugees or forcibly displaced youth.
existing.notes: Admissions and funding are two separate applications: a student must first obtain an offer of admission to UCT and then apply for the programme, and only admitted students can be awarded it. Part-time study and qualifications by research only (Master's by dissertation or PhD) are not covered. Students admitted to the Integrated Master's Programme through ACDI or Healthy Futures South Africa are also eligible.
existing.application_period: 2027 intake; undergraduate applications closed 30 September 2026, postgraduate applications remain open until 31 October 2026
existing.program_type: Foundation-funded need-based scholarship administered by a university
